common_name: Picasso Calla Lily (White with Deep Purple Throat)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes after last frost in rich, moist, well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun; Picasso bears white spathes with a dramatic deep purple throat that bleeds partway up the petal edges.

directions: Plant rhizomes after last frost in rich, moist, well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun, siting it where hot afternoon sun will not scorch the foliage in warm climates. Picasso bears elegant, funnel-shaped spathes in creamy white with a striking, deep purple-violet throat that bleeds a thin margin of color up the petal edges, a bold two-tone effect that has made it one of the most popular colored calla lily hybrids. Narrow, glossy green leaves rise from the rhizome through summer, and the plant goes dormant in fall. In zones 8-10 it can be left dry in the ground through a mild winter, while in colder climates the rhizomes should be lifted and stored dry like dahlia tubers. Reduce watering as foliage yellows in fall to encourage the plant into its natural dormant period.
